current_example.title: Example: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of an NxN Matrix

q-38665.name: Question 1
q-38665.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
q-38665.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=-2\pm 5\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=-7.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ ∓2\text{i} \\ 1∓\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

q-38665.html:
Question 1
?

P=[1−2050−201−1],B=[−7000−250−5−2]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=5±2i and v=[2i∓2i1∓i]
b
λ=1±5i and v=[−2∓2i1∓i]
c
λ=−2±5i and v=[−21±2i∓i]
d
λ=5±2i and v=[−2±2 1∓i]
e
λ=−2±5i and v=[−2∓2i1∓i]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 3×3 real matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

  • From our block diagonal matrix B=[−7000−250−5−2], we deduce the complex eigenvalues are λ2,3=−2±5i and the real eigenvalue is λ1=−7.

  • From our matrix P=[1−2050−201−1], we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are v2,3=[−2∓2i1∓i],v1=[150].

q-135467.name: Question 2
q-135467.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & -7 & 0 \\ 5 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 & 0 \\ -3 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
q-135467.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 3 & 0 \\ -3 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1,2}=8\pm 3\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{3}=5.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & -7 & 0 \\ 5 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{1,2}=[\begin{aligned}1\pm 4\text{i} \\ ∓7\text{i} \\ 5\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

q-135467.html:
Question 2
?

P=[1450−7053−2],B=[830−380005]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=8±3i and v=[1±4i∓7i5±3i]
b
λ=3±8i and v=[1∓4i∓7i3±5i]
c
λ=5±3i and v=[−1±4i∓7i5±3i]
d
λ=−8±3i and v=[1±4i±7i−5±3i]
e
λ=8±5i and v=[5±i∓7i5∓3i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 3×3 real matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

  • From our block diagonal matrix B=[830−380005], we deduce the complex eigenvalues are λ1,2=8±3i and the real eigenvalue is λ3=5.

  • From our matrix P=[1450−7053−2], we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are v1,2=[1±4i∓7i5±3i],v3=[50−2].
q-135467.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Corresponding Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Block Diagonal Form

q-135440.name: Question 3
q-135440.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
q-135440.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=3\pm 4\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=4.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1∓2\text{i} \\ 5\pm 4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

q-135440.html:
Question 3
?

P=[240−3−1−2054],B=[4000340−43]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=1±4i and v=[4−1±2i−5±4i]
b
λ=3±i and v=[2−1∓4i5±2i]
c
λ=4±3i and v=[−4−1∓2i5∓4i]
d
λ=−3±4i and v=[11∓2i5±4i]
e
λ=3±4i and v=[4−1∓2i5±4i]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 3×3 real matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

  • From our block diagonal matrix B=[4000340−43], we deduce the complex eigenvalues are λ2,3=3±4i and the real eigenvalue is λ1=4.

  • From our matrix P=[240−3−1−2054], we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are v2,3=[4−1∓2i5±4i],v1=[2−30].

q-38917.name: Question 4
q-38917.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 4 & 6 & 5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & -8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
q-38917.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & -8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1,2}=-8\pm 2\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{3}=5.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 4 & 6 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{1,2}=[\begin{aligned}1\pm 2\text{i} \\ \pm \text{i} \\ 4\pm 6\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

q-135441.name: Question 5
q-135441.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
q-135441.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=5\pm 7\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=-1.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}4\pm 6\text{i} \\ ∓2\text{i} \\ 5\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

q-135441.html:
Question 5
?

P=[246−30−2153],B=[−1000570−75]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=5±7i and v=[4±6i∓2i5±3i]
b
λ=7±5i and v=[2±6i±2i3±5i]
c
λ=−5±7i and v=[−4∓6i∓2i1±5i]
d
λ=−5±i and v=[2±6i∓i3∓5i]
e
λ=5±i and v=[−4±6i∓2i5∓3i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 3×3 real matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

  • From our block diagonal matrix B=[−1000570−75], we deduce the complex eigenvalues are λ2,3=5±7i and the real eigenvalue is λ1=−1.

  • From our matrix P=[246−30−2153], we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are v2,3=[4±6i∓2i5±3i],v1=[2−31].
q-135441.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues and Corresponding Eigenvectors of a Matrix in Block Diagonal Form

q-135534.name: Question 6
q-135534.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 5 \\ 8 & 4 & 3 \\ -5 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
q-135534.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & 5 \\ 8 & 4-\lambda  & 3 \\ -5 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )^{2}-5(-5)) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +29) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=4.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{(4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 29}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{-100}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm 10\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-2\pm 5\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

q-135471.name: Question 7
q-135471.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 2 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ -4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
q-135471.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}6-\lambda  & 0 & 2 \\ 8 & 3-\lambda  & 1 \\ -4 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )((6-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-2(-4)) & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-8\lambda +20) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=3.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{8\pm \sqrt{(-8)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 20}}{2} \\  & =\frac{8\pm \sqrt{-16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{8\pm 4\text{i}}{2} \\  & =4\pm 2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

q-135531.name: Question 8
q-135531.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & 6 \\ -4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
q-135531.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-7-\lambda  & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & -2-\lambda  & 6 \\ -4 & 0 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )((-7-\lambda )(-3-\lambda )-5(-4)) & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+10\lambda +41) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=-2.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-10\pm \sqrt{(10)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 41}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-10\pm \sqrt{-64}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-10\pm 8\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-5\pm 4\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 4 \\ 0 & -4 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

To compute the eigenvalues of A, we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

det(A−λI)=0|−7−λ051−2−λ6−40−3−λ|=0(−2−λ)((−7−λ)(−3−λ)−5(−4))=0(−2−λ)(λ2+10λ+41)=0.

So, the real eigenvalue is λ1=−2. Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

λ2,3=−10±(10)2−4⋅1⋅412=−10±−642=−10±8i2=−5±4i. Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

B=[−2000−540−4−5].

q-38914.name: Question 9
q-38914.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -13 \\ -6 & -7 & 8 \\ 2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
q-38914.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 0 & -13 \\ -6 & -7-\lambda  & 8 \\ 2 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-7-\lambda )((4-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-2(-13)) & =0 \\ (-7-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-6\lambda +34) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=-7.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{6\pm \sqrt{(-6)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 34}}{2} \\  & =\frac{6\pm \sqrt{-100}}{2} \\  & =\frac{6\pm 10\text{i}}{2} \\  & =3\pm 5\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 9
?

A=[40−13−6−78202] Consider the matrix A shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix B, where the 2×2 block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that A=PBP−1.

a
B=[3000370−73]
b
B=[−7000530−35]
c
B=[3000−750−5−7]
d
B=[3000−750−5−7]
e
B=[−7000350−53]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

To compute the eigenvalues of A, we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

det(A−λI)=0|4−λ0−13−6−7−λ8202−λ|=0(−7−λ)((4−λ)(2−λ)−2(−13))=0(−7−λ)(λ2−6λ+34)=0.

So, the real eigenvalue is λ1=−7. Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

λ2,3=6±(−6)2−4⋅1⋅342=6±−1002=6±10i2=3±5i. Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

B=[−7000350−53].

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$
q-135519.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & -4-\lambda  & 2 \\ -5 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )((1-\lambda )^{2}-5(-5)) & =0 \\ (-4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +26) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
${\lambda }_{1}=-4.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{(-2)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 26}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2\pm \sqrt{-100}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2\pm 10\text{i}}{2} \\  & =1\pm 5\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

A=[1053−42−501] Consider the matrix A shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix B, where the 2×2 block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that A=PBP−1.

a
B=[−5000140−41]

EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

To compute the eigenvalues of A, we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

det(A−λI)=0|1−λ053−4−λ2−501−λ|=0(−4−λ)((1−λ)2−5(−5))=0(−4−λ)(λ2−2λ+26)=0.

So, the real eigenvalue is λ1=−4. Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

λ2,3=2±(−2)2−4⋅1⋅262=2±−1002=2±10i2=1±5i. Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

B=[−4000150−51].

q-38660.name: Question 11
q-38660.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5+7\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} \\ \text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1-2\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-2,$  respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-38660.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 7 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

q-38660.html:
Question 11
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[5+7i1+ii],v3=[10−2],B=[−1−202−1000−2] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=−1−2i and λ3=−2, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[75111010−2]
b
[157011−201]
c
[5171010−21]
d
[175011−211]
e
[57111001−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ3 with corresponding eigenvector v3, and two complex eigenvalues λ1=λ―2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1=v―2, then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)0−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)000λ3],P=[|||Re(v1)Im(v1)v3|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[−1−202−1000−2], we deduce that the first and second columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v3:

P=[57111001−2]

q-135662.name: Question 12
q-135662.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ -6+3\text{i} \\ -5\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=7$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=4+8\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-135662.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & -8 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{1}$ and the second and third columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{2}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & -6 & 3 \\ -3 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

q-135662.html:
Question 12
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v2 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[40−3],v2=[1−i−6+3i−5i],B=[7000480−84] The vectors v1 and v2 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=7 and λ2=4+8i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[4−10063−302]
b
[21−10−6−3−10−5]
c
[412203−32−5]
d
[41−10−36−35−5]
e
[41−10−63−30−5]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[7000480−84], we deduce that the first column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v1 and the second and third columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v2:

P=[41−10−63−30−5]

q-135660.name: Question 13
q-135660.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4-\text{i} \\ -5\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 0 \\ -6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4+6\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-1,$  respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-135660.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 0 \\ -6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

q-135660.html:
Question 13
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[4−i−5i3−2i],v3=[1−34],B=[460−64000−1] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=4+6i and λ3=−1, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[4−113−5−3301]
b
[4−100−2−3350]
c
[4−110−54−2−20]
d
[5−11−2−5−31−20]
e
[4−110−5−33−24]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ3 with corresponding eigenvector v3, and two complex eigenvalues λ1=λ―2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1=v―2, then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)0−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)000λ3],P=[|||Re(v1)Im(v1)v3|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[460−64000−1], we deduce that the first and second columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v3:

P=[4−110−5−33−24]

q-38885.name: Question 14
q-38885.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2+3\text{i} \\ 1+4\text{i} \\ 6\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=3+5\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-38885.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first column of $P$ correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the second and third columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{2}.$ Therefore, 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 5 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[2000350−53], we deduce that the first column of P correspond to the real eigenvector v1, and the second and third columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v2. Therefore,

q-135643.name: Question 15
q-135643.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3+5\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} \\ 4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 0 \\ -8 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=2+8\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-5,$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-135643.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 0 \\ -8 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Question 15
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where the 2×2 block of B represents a rotation-scaling matrix: v1=[3+5i1−6i4i],v3=[521],B=[280−82000−5] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=2+8i and λ3=−5, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[3551−62041]
b
[3532−6001−4]
c
[552102−641]
d
[3515−65046]
e
[325162140]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a real 3×3 matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ3 with corresponding eigenvector v3, and two complex eigenvalues λ1=λ―2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1=v―2, then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)0−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)000λ3],P=[|||Re(v1)Im(v1)v3|||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[280−82000−5], we deduce that the first and second columns of P will correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third column of P will correspond to the real eigenvector v3:

P=[3551−62041]

q-135539.name: Question 16
q-135539.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1+4\text{i} \\ -6+\text{i} \\ 5+\text{i} \\ 3-3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1+5\text{i} \\ -4-4\text{i} \\ 1+3\text{i} \\ -5-3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-2-2\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=4\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-135539.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 & 1 & 5 \\ -6 & 1 & -4 & -4 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & -3 & -5 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 16
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where both 2×2 blocks of B represent rotation-scaling matrices: v1=[−1+4i−6+i5+i3−3i],v3=[1+5i−4−4i1+3i−5−3i],B=[−2−2002−200000400−40] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=−2−2i and λ3=4i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[4−1151−6−4−41513−33−5−3]
b
[−14153−3−5−35113−61−4−4]
c
[−61−4−45113−14153−3−5−3]
d
[−1415−61−4−451133−3−5−3]
e
[−61−4−45131−14513−3−3−5]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 4×4 real matrix that has complex eigenvalues

λ1=λ―2 and λ3=λ―4

with corresponding eigenvectors

v1=v―2 and v3=v―4,

then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)00−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)0000Re(λ3)Im(λ3)00−Im(λ3)Re(λ3)] and P=[||||Re(v1)Im(v1)Re(v3)Im(v3)||||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[−2−2002−200000400−40], we deduce that the first and second columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third and forth columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v3. Therefore, P=[−1415−61−4−451133−3−5−3].

q-135535.name: Question 17
q-135535.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-5-\text{i} \\ -2+5\text{i} \\ -4+3\text{i} \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}4+4\text{i} \\ 1-5\text{i} \\ 4-6\text{i} \\ 1-4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1-2\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-4-\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-135535.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -1 & 4 & 4 \\ -2 & 5 & 1 & -5 \\ -4 & 3 & 4 & -6 \\ 5 & 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[−5−144−251−5−434−6501−4]
b
[−251−5−5−144501−4−434−6]
c
[−5−144501−4−434−6−251−5]
d
[−251−5−434−6−5−144501−4]
e
[−1−5445−21−53−44−6051−4]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 4×4 real matrix that has complex eigenvalues

λ1=λ―2 and λ3=λ―4

with corresponding eigenvectors

v1=v―2 and v3=v―4,

then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)00−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)0000Re(λ3)Im(λ3)00−Im(λ3)Re(λ3)] and P=[||||Re(v1)Im(v1)Re(v3)Im(v3)||||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[−1−2002−10000−4−1001−4], we deduce that the first and second columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third and forth columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v3. Therefore, P=[−5−144−251−5−434−6501−4].

q-38921.name: Question 18
q-38921.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1+\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 6-2\text{i} \\ 2+\text{i} \\ 1+\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=3-2\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-1-5\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-38921.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

q-38921.html:
Question 18
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where both 2×2 blocks of B represent rotation-scaling matrices: v1=[11+i1+i1],v3=[−36−2i2+i1+i],B=[3−200230000−1−5005−1] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=3−2i and λ3=−1−5i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[01−30116−211210111]
b
[116−210−3010111121]
c
[10−3010111121116−2]
d
[10−30116−211211011]
e
[116−2112110−301011]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 4×4 real matrix that has complex eigenvalues

λ1=λ―2 and λ3=λ―4

with corresponding eigenvectors

v1=v―2 and v3=v―4,

then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)00−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)0000Re(λ3)Im(λ3)00−Im(λ3)Re(λ3)] and P=[||||Re(v1)Im(v1)Re(v3)Im(v3)||||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[3−200230000−1−5005−1], we deduce that the first and second columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third and forth columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v3. Therefore, P=[10−30116−211211011].

q-135540.name: Question 19
q-135540.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-7+2\text{i} \\ -2-7\text{i} \\ -2-2\text{i} \\ -3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}5-5\text{i} \\ -7 \\ -2+3\text{i} \\ -5-5\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=2+\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-135540.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 & 5 & -5 \\ -2 & -7 & -7 & 0 \\ -2 & -2 & -2 & 3 \\ -3 & -2 & -5 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 19
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where both 2×2 blocks of B represent rotation-scaling matrices: v1=[−7+2i−2−7i−2−2i−3−2i],v3=[5−5i−7−2+3i−5−5i],B=[0400−4000002100−12] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=4i and λ3=2+i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[−2−70−7−2−23−2−72−55−3−2−5−5]
b
[−2−7−70−725−5−3−2−5−5−2−2−23]
c
[−725−5−3−2−5−5−2−2−23−2−7−70]
d
[−2−7−70−2−2−23−725−5−3−2−5−5]
e
[−725−5−2−7−70−2−2−23−3−2−5−5]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 4×4 real matrix that has complex eigenvalues

λ1=λ―2 and λ3=λ―4

with corresponding eigenvectors

v1=v―2 and v3=v―4,

then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)00−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)0000Re(λ3)Im(λ3)00−Im(λ3)Re(λ3)] and P=[||||Re(v1)Im(v1)Re(v3)Im(v3)||||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[0400−4000002100−12], we deduce that the first and second columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third and forth columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v3. Therefore, P=[−725−5−2−7−70−2−2−23−3−2−5−5].

q-135537.name: Question 20
q-135537.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3+\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i} \\ 2+4\text{i} \\ 3-4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4-7\text{i} \\ 1-2\text{i} \\ 3+\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-5+\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-3\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
q-135537.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & -2 & 4 & -7 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & -4 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

q-135537.html:
Question 20
?

Consider the vectors v1 and v3 and the block diagonal matrix B shown below, where both 2×2 blocks of B represent rotation-scaling matrices: v1=[−3+i5−2i2+4i3−4i],v3=[24−7i1−2i3+i],B=[−5100−1−500000−30030] The vectors v1 and v3 are the eigenvectors of a matrix A corresponding to the eigenvalues λ1=−5+i and λ3=−3i, respectively. Given that A=PBP−1, which of the following could be the matrix P?

a
[5−24−7−31203−431241−2]
b
[−31205−24−7241−23−431]
c
[5−2−7424−21−31023−413]
d
[1−320−254−7421−2−4331]
e
[−31203−431241−25−24−7]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 4×4 real matrix that has complex eigenvalues

λ1=λ―2 and λ3=λ―4

with corresponding eigenvectors

v1=v―2 and v3=v―4,

then A=PBP−1, where B=[Re(λ1)Im(λ1)00−Im(λ1)Re(λ1)0000Re(λ3)Im(λ3)00−Im(λ3)Re(λ3)] and P=[||||Re(v1)Im(v1)Re(v3)Im(v3)||||]. Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

From our block diagonal matrix B=[−5100−1−500000−30030], we deduce that the first and second columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v1, and the third and forth columns of P correspond to the complex eigenvector v3. Therefore, P=[−31205−24−7241−23−431].
